//alerts: `alertsChannel` is the seam's own name for its door, in an import clause — code the sweep reads though the specifier beside it is subtracted. The channel arrives as a declared service on a component of its own (`src/browser.tsx`'s `notices`), and the local binding is `noticeChannel` so the word is spelled once, where the exporter spells it.
//chat: Two spellings and neither reaches for the chat package's code. In the browser half it is `olai-plugin-chat/dock`'s exported tag name in an import clause, with the live panel door arriving as a declared service on a component of its own. In the server half it is the KEY `chat.conversations` and the prose around it: a key is a name the runtime resolves, which is exactly what makes this row able to run with chat switched off. In the page it is the word in `Chats`, the sidebar heading a person is pointed at when this viewport has no seat to dock a conversation in.
//files: The English plural of a file, in prose a person reads and in the name of the list of three the folder holds — `PLUGIN_FILES`, `2 files, 38 lines` on the page, the sentence that says which three there are. None of them reaches the files row.
//markdown: `Markdown` is the shared renderer component the README is drawn through (`@olai/markdown-ui`), not a runtime lookup of the markdown row.
//mcp: The writer a file written through the agent's own verb is attributed to, which is the door that write came through (`@olai/format`'s `Writer`). It is the ledger's word for an author, not the mcp row.
//navigation: `Navigation` is the type on navigation's own contract door, named in an import clause and in the holder it types. The live router arrives as a declared service on the `palette` component; the page, the section and the alert read this package's own hold on it.
//search: `search` is the palette row's own key — the lowercase haystack every contributed row carries (`PaletteItem.search`) — and not the search row.
//settings: The FILE a plugin's consent and knobs are kept in — `_olai/Settings.olai` — named in the page's heading, in the agent's layout answer and in the words the tools use to say where a person's yes is written down. It is a vault file, not the settings row.
//sidebar: The slot a section is hung in is called `sidebar.section` by the row that owns it; naming a slot is how a face is contributed at all.
//trash: The vault's own write op (`{ op: "trash", id }`) — what removing a plugin does with the node its consent was written on, named where that write is spelled. It is the format's verb for moving a record to `_olai/Trash.olai`, not the trash row.
//vault: This row IS the vault's plugins, so the word is in its own name, its own tool names (`vault-plugins_run`), its package path and the prose a person reads: `Kept in your vault as plugins/<word>/`. The vault row is reached the way every other row is, through a declared service. In the alert it is the sentence a folder somebody copied in is announced with — `It is in your vault and nobody has read it yet` — which is prose about a directory.
